passages.text: Then the word of the LORD came to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha, saying: “Even though I lifted you out of the dust and made you ruler over My people Israel, you have walked in the way of Jeroboam and have caused My people Israel to sin and to provoke Me to anger by their sins.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Jehu son of Hanani about Baasha.
The LORD said these words against Baasha.
The LORD said, “I lifted you out of the dust.
I made you ruler over My people Israel.
But you walked in the way of Jeroboam.
You caused My people Israel to sin.
You made them sin and provoke Me to anger by their sins.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֤י דְבַר־ יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ יֵה֣וּא בֶן־ חֲנָ֔נִי עַל־ בַּעְשָׁ֖א לֵאמֹֽר׃ יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֲרִימֹתִ֙יךָ֙ מִן־ הֶ֣עָפָ֔ר וָאֶתֶּנְךָ֣ נָגִ֔יד עַ֖ל עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַתֵּ֣לֶךְ׀ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ יָרָבְעָ֗ם וַֽתַּחֲטִא֙ אֶת־ עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְהַכְעִיסֵ֖נִי בְּחַטֹּאתָֽם׃

passages.text: So now I will consume Baasha and his house, and I will make your house like that of Jeroboam son of Nebat: Anyone belonging to Baasha who dies in the city will be eaten by dogs, and anyone who dies in the field will be eaten by the birds of the air.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Baasha through the prophet Jehu son of Hanani.
God said He would destroy Baasha and his family.
God said He would make Baasha’s house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat.
God said anyone from Baasha’s family who died in the city would be eaten by dogs.
God said anyone from Baasha’s family who died in the field would be eaten by the birds of the air.
passages.original: הִנְנִ֥י מַבְעִ֛יר אַחֲרֵ֥י בַעְשָׁ֖א וְאַחֲרֵ֣י בֵית֑וֹ וְנָֽתַתִּי֙ אֶת־ בֵּ֣יתְךָ֔ כְּבֵ֖ית יָרָבְעָ֥ם בֶּן־ נְבָֽט׃ הַמֵּ֤ת לְבַעְשָׁא֙ בָּעִ֔יר יֹֽאכְל֖וּ הַכְּלָבִ֑ים וְהַמֵּ֥ת לוֹ֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה יֹאכְל֖וּ ע֥וֹף הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

passages.text: As for the rest of the acts of Baasha, along with his accomplishments and might, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
passages.sermon:
Baasha was a king of Israel.
He did many things during his reign.
He accomplished much.
He showed strength and might.
The rest of Baasha’s acts are recorded.
They are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
passages.original: וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י בַעְשָׁ֛א וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה וּגְבֽוּרָת֑וֹ הֲלֹא־ הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־ סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: And Baasha rested with his fathers and was buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah reigned in his place.
passages.sermon:
Baasha was king of Israel.
Baasha died.
People buried Baasha in Tirzah.
Elah was Baasha’s son.
Elah became king after Baasha.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב בַּעְשָׁא֙ עִם־ אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקָּבֵ֖ר בְּתִרְצָ֑ה וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֵלָ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃

passages.text: Moreover, the word of the LORD came through the prophet Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha and his house, because of all the evil he had done in the sight of the LORD, provoking Him to anger with the work of his hands and becoming like the house of Jeroboam, and also because Baasha had struck down the house of Jeroboam.
passages.sermon:
Jehu was a prophet.  
Jehu was the son of Hanani.  
The LORD spoke through Jehu.  
The LORD gave a message against Baasha.  
The LORD gave a message against Baasha’s house.  
Baasha did evil things.  
Baasha did these things where the LORD could see.  
Baasha made the LORD angry.  
Baasha made the LORD angry by what he did.  
Baasha’s actions were like the house of Jeroboam.  
Baasha became like the house of Jeroboam.  
Baasha also struck down the house of Jeroboam.  
The LORD’s message came because of these things.
passages.original: וְגַ֡ם בְּיַד־ יֵה֨וּא בֶן־ חֲנָ֜נִי הַנָּבִ֗יא דְּבַר־ יְהוָ֡ה הָיָה֩ אֶל־ בַּעְשָׁ֨א וְאֶל־ בֵּית֜וֹ וְעַ֥ל כָּל־ הָרָעָ֣ה׀ אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֣ה׀ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה לְהַכְעִיסוֹ֙ בְּמַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יָדָ֔יו לִהְי֖וֹת כְּבֵ֣ית יָרָבְעָ֑ם וְעַ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ הִכָּ֖ה אֹתֽוֹ׃פ

passages.text: In the twenty-sixth year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Elah son of Baasha became king of Israel, and he reigned in Tirzah two years.
passages.sermon:
Asa was king of Judah.
He ruled for many years.
In the twenty-sixth year of Asa’s reign, Elah became king.
Elah was the son of Baasha.
Elah ruled over Israel.
He ruled in the city of Tirzah.
Elah was king for two years.
passages.original: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וָשֵׁשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לְאָסָ֖א מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָ֠לַךְ אֵלָ֨ה בֶן־ בַּעְשָׁ֧א עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בְּתִרְצָ֖ה שְׁנָתָֽיִם׃

passages.text: However, while Elah was in Tirzah getting drunk in the house of Arza the steward of his household there, Elah’s servant Zimri, the commander of half his chariots, conspired against him.
passages.sermon:
Elah was king of Israel.
Elah was in the city of Tirzah.
Elah was drinking and became drunk.
He was in the house of Arza.
Arza was the steward over Elah’s household in Tirzah.
Zimri was Elah’s servant.
Zimri was the commander of half of Elah’s chariots.
Zimri conspired against Elah.
passages.original: וַיִּקְשֹׁ֤ר עָלָיו֙ עַבְדּ֣וֹ זִמְרִ֔י שַׂ֖ר מַחֲצִ֣ית הָרָ֑כֶב וְה֤וּא בְתִרְצָה֙ שֹׁתֶ֣ה שִׁכּ֔וֹר בֵּ֣ית אַרְצָ֔א אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־ הַבַּ֖יִת בְּתִרְצָֽה׃

passages.text: So in the twenty-seventh year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Zimri went in, struck Elah down, and killed him. And Zimri reigned in his place.
passages.sermon:
Asa was king of Judah.
He had reigned for twenty-seven years.
Elah was king of Israel at that time.
Zimri was a servant of Elah.
Zimri went in to Elah.
Zimri struck Elah down.
Zimri killed Elah.
Zimri became king after Elah.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֤א זִמְרִי֙ וַיַּכֵּ֣הוּ וַיְמִיתֵ֔הוּ בִּשְׁנַת֙ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים וָשֶׁ֔בַע לְאָסָ֖א מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּמְלֹ֖ךְ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃

passages.text: As soon as Zimri began to reign and was seated on the throne, he struck down the entire household of Baasha. He did not leave a single male, whether a kinsman or friend.
passages.sermon:
Zimri was a commander of half the chariots of King Elah of Israel.
Zimri killed Elah and became king in his place.
As soon as Zimri became king and sat on the throne, he acted.
Zimri struck down the entire household of Baasha.
He did not leave a single male alive from Baasha’s family.
He killed every male relative of Baasha.
He also killed every male friend of Baasha.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֨י בְמָלְכ֜וֹ כְּשִׁבְתּ֣וֹ עַל־ כִּסְא֗וֹ הִכָּה֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ בֵּ֣ית בַּעְשָׁ֔א לֹֽא־ הִשְׁאִ֥יר ל֖וֹ מַשְׁתִּ֣ין בְּקִ֑יר וְגֹאֲלָ֖יו וְרֵעֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: So Zimri destroyed the entire household of Baasha, according to the word that the LORD had spoken against Baasha through Jehu the prophet.
passages.sermon:
Zimri was a king of Israel.
Zimri destroyed every person in the household of Baasha.
The LORD had spoken a word against Baasha.
The LORD spoke this word through Jehu the prophet.
Zimri destroyed Baasha’s household as the LORD had said.
passages.original: וַיַּשְׁמֵ֣ד זִמְרִ֔י אֵ֖ת כָּל־ בֵּ֣ית בַּעְשָׁ֑א כִּדְבַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר אֶל־ בַּעְשָׁ֔א בְּיַ֖ד יֵה֥וּא הַנָּבִֽיא׃

passages.text: This happened because of all the sins Baasha and his son Elah had committed and had caused Israel to commit, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger with their worthless idols.
passages.sermon:
Baasha was king of Israel.
Elah was Baasha’s son.
Baasha sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel.
Elah also sinned against the LORD.
Baasha and Elah led Israel into sin.
They caused the people of Israel to sin.
They made Israel worship worthless idols.
These sins made the LORD angry.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
Baasha and Elah provoked the LORD to anger by their actions.
passages.original: אֶ֚ל כָּל־ חַטֹּ֣אות בַּעְשָׁ֔א וְחַטֹּ֖אות אֵלָ֣ה בְנ֑וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטְא֗וּ וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר הֶחֱטִ֙יאוּ֙ אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְהַכְעִ֗יס אֶת־ יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּהַבְלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: As for the rest of the acts of Elah, along with all his accomplishments, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
passages.sermon:
Elah was a king of Israel.
He did many things during his reign.
The rest of Elah’s deeds are recorded.
All his accomplishments are written down.
They are found in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
passages.original: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י אֵלָ֖ה וְכָל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֽוֹא־ הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־ סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

passages.text: In the twenty-seventh year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Zimri reigned in Tirzah for seven days. Now the troops were encamped against Gibbethon of the Philistines, and the people in the camp heard that Zimri had not only conspired but had also struck down the king. So there in the camp that very day, all Israel proclaimed Omri, the commander of the army, king over Israel.
passages.sermon:
Asa was king of Judah.
In the twenty-seventh year of Asa’s reign, Zimri became king.
Zimri ruled in Tirzah.
He reigned for seven days.
At that time, the Israelite army camped near Gibbethon.
Gibbethon belonged to the Philistines.
The people in the camp heard news about Zimri.
They heard that Zimri had conspired against the king.
They also heard that Zimri had killed the king.
All Israel was in the camp that day.
The people made Omri king over Israel.
Omri was the commander of the army.
passages.original: בִּשְׁנַת֩ עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וָשֶׁ֜בַע שָׁנָ֗ה לְאָסָא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה מָלַ֥ךְ זִמְרִ֛י שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים בְּתִרְצָ֑ה וְהָעָ֣ם חֹנִ֔ים עַֽל־ גִּבְּת֖וֹן אֲשֶׁ֥ר לַפְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃ וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע הָעָם֙ הַחֹנִ֣ים לֵאמֹ֔ר קָשַׁ֣ר זִמְרִ֔י וְגַ֖ם הִכָּ֣ה אֶת־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיַּמְלִ֣כוּ כָֽל־ יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל אֶת־ עָמְרִ֨י שַׂר־ צָבָ֧א עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא בַּֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

passages.text: Then Omri and all the Israelites marched up from Gibbethon and besieged Tirzah.
passages.sermon:
Omri was the commander of the army of Israel.
All the Israelites followed Omri.
They marched up from Gibbethon.
They went to Tirzah.
They surrounded Tirzah and laid siege to it.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲלֶ֥ה עָמְרִ֛י וְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל עִמּ֖וֹ מִֽגִּבְּת֑וֹן וַיָּצֻ֖רוּ עַל־ תִּרְצָֽה׃

passages.text: When Zimri saw that the city was captured, he entered the citadel of the royal palace and burned it down upon himself. So he died because of the sins he had committed, doing evil in the sight of the LORD and following the example of Jeroboam and the sin he had committed and had caused Israel to commit.
passages.sermon:
Zimri was king of Israel.
Zimri saw that the city was captured.
He entered the citadel of the royal palace.
He set fire to the royal palace.
He burned it down upon himself.
Zimri died in the fire.
He died because of his sins.
He did evil in the sight of the LORD.
He followed the example of Jeroboam.
Jeroboam sinned and led Israel into sin.
Zimri also caused Israel to sin.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֞י כִּרְא֤וֹת זִמְרִי֙ כִּֽי־ נִלְכְּדָ֣ה הָעִ֔יר וַיָּבֹ֖א אֶל־ אַרְמ֣וֹן בֵּית־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיִּשְׂרֹ֨ף עָלָ֧יו אֶת־ בֵּֽית־ מֶ֛לֶךְ בָּאֵ֖שׁ וַיָּמֹֽת׃ עַל־ חַטָּאתוֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטָ֔א לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה לָלֶ֙כֶת֙ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ יָרָבְעָ֔ם וּבְחַטָּאתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה לְהַחֲטִ֖יא אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: As for the rest of the acts of Zimri and the treason he committed, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
passages.sermon:
Zimri was a king of Israel.
He committed treason.
He did other acts during his life.
The Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel records these things.
This book contains the rest of Zimri’s acts and his treason.
passages.original: וְיֶ֙תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י זִמְרִ֔י וְקִשְׁר֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר קָשָׁ֑ר הֲלֹֽא־ הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־ סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

passages.text: At that time the people of Israel were divided: Half of the people supported Tibni son of Ginath as king, and half supported Omri.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel became divided.
This happened at that time.
Half of the people followed Tibni.
Tibni was the son of Ginath.
They wanted Tibni to be king.
The other half of the people followed Omri.
They wanted Omri to be king.
passages.original: אָ֧ז יֵחָלֵ֛ק הָעָ֥ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לַחֵ֑צִי חֲצִ֨י הָעָ֜ם הָ֠יָה אַחֲרֵ֨י תִבְנִ֤י בֶן־ גִּינַת֙ לְהַמְלִיכ֔וֹ וְהַחֲצִ֖י אַחֲרֵ֥י עָמְרִֽי׃

passages.text: But the followers of Omri proved stronger than those of Tibni son of Ginath. So Tibni died and Omri became king.
passages.sermon:
Omri was a leader in Israel.
Tibni son of Ginath was also a leader in Israel.
Some people followed Omri.
Some people followed Tibni.
The people who followed Omri became stronger.
The people who followed Tibni became weaker.
Tibni died.
Omri became king.
passages.original: וַיֶּחֱזַ֤ק הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַחֲרֵ֣י עָמְרִ֔י אֶת־ הָעָ֕ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַחֲרֵ֖י תִּבְנִ֣י בֶן־ גִּינַ֑ת וַיָּ֣מָת תִּבְנִ֔י וַיִּמְלֹ֖ךְ עָמְרִֽי׃פ

passages.text: In the thirty-first year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Omri became king of Israel, and he reigned twelve years, six of them in Tirzah.
passages.sermon:
Omri became king of Israel.
This happened in the thirty-first year of Asa’s reign over Judah.
Omri ruled Israel for twelve years.
He ruled six of those years in Tirzah.
passages.original: בִּשְׁנַת֩ שְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים וְאַחַ֜ת שָׁנָ֗ה לְאָסָא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה מָלַ֤ךְ עָמְרִי֙ עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָ֑ה בְּתִרְצָ֖ה מָלַ֥ךְ שֵׁשׁ־ שָׁנִֽים׃

passages.text: He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver and built a city there, calling it Samaria after the name of Shemer, who had owned the hill.
passages.sermon:
Omri was king of Israel.
Omri bought a hill from a man named Shemer.
He paid Shemer two talents of silver for the hill.
Omri built a city on the hill.
He named the city Samaria.
He named it after Shemer, who had owned the hill.
passages.original: וַיִּ֜קֶן אֶת־ הָהָ֥ר שֹׁמְר֛וֹן מֵ֥אֶת שֶׁ֖מֶר בְּכִכְּרַ֣יִם כָּ֑סֶף וַיִּ֙בֶן֙ אֶת־ הָהָ֔ר וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֶת־ שֵׁ֤ם הָעִיר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּנָ֔ה עַ֣ל שֶׁם־ שֶׁ֔מֶר אֲדֹנֵ֖י הָהָ֥ר שֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃

passages.text: But Omri did evil in the sight of the LORD and acted more wickedly than all who were before him.
passages.sermon:
Omri was king of Israel.
Omri did evil.
The LORD saw Omri’s evil.
Omri was more wicked than all the kings before him.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה עָמְרִ֛י הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיָּ֕רַע מִכֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְפָנָֽיו׃

passages.text: For he walked in all the ways of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sins, which he caused Israel to commit, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger with their worthless idols.
passages.sermon:
Omri was king of Israel.
Omri followed the example of Jeroboam son of Nebat.
Jeroboam led Israel into sin.
Omri committed the same sins as Jeroboam.
Omri caused Israel to sin.
Omri made the LORD, the God of Israel, angry.
Omri and Israel worshiped worthless idols.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ בְּכָל־ דֶּ֙רֶךְ֙ יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־ נְבָ֔ט וּבְחַטֹּאתָיו אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶחֱטִ֖יא אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לְהַכְעִ֗יס אֶת־ יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּהַבְלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: As for the rest of the acts of Omri, along with his accomplishments and the might he exercised, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
passages.sermon:
Omri was king of Israel.
He did many things.
He showed great strength.
The rest of Omri’s deeds are recorded.
His accomplishments and his might are written down.
They are in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
passages.original: וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֤י עָמְרִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וּגְבוּרָת֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֹֽא־ הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־ סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: And Omri rested with his fathers and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab reigned in his place.
passages.sermon:
Omri was king of Israel.
Omri died.
People buried Omri in Samaria.
Ahab was Omri’s son.
Ahab became king after Omri.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב עָמְרִי֙ עִם־ אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקָּבֵ֖ר בְּשֹׁמְר֑וֹן וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אַחְאָ֥ב בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ

passages.text: In the thirty-eighth year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel, and he reigned in Samaria twenty-two years.
passages.sermon:
Ahab was the son of Omri.
Ahab became king of Israel.
Asa was king of Judah at that time.
Ahab began to reign in the thirty-eighth year of Asa’s rule over Judah.
Ahab ruled Israel from Samaria.
Ahab reigned for twenty-two years.
passages.original: וְאַחְאָ֣ב בֶּן־ עָמְרִ֗י מָלַךְ֙ עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וּשְׁמֹנֶה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לְאָסָ֖א מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַ֠יִּמְלֹךְ אַחְאָ֨ב בֶּן־ עָמְרִ֤י עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וּשְׁתַּ֖יִם שָׁנָֽה׃

passages.text: However, Ahab son of Omri did evil in the sight of the LORD, more than all who were before him.
passages.sermon:
Ahab was the son of Omri.
Ahab became king of Israel.
Ahab did evil things.
The LORD saw Ahab’s actions.
Ahab did more evil than all the kings before him.
passages.original: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ אַחְאָ֧ב בֶּן־ עָמְרִ֛י הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה מִכֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְפָנָֽיו׃

passages.text: And as if it were not enough for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, he even married Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and he then proceeded to serve and worship Baal.
passages.sermon:
Ahab was the son of Omri.
Ahab became king of Israel.
Ahab did evil in the sight of the LORD.
Ahab followed the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat.
Ahab did not think these sins were serious.
Ahab married Jezebel.
Jezebel was the daughter of Ethbaal.
Ethbaal was king of the Sidonians.
Ahab began to serve Baal.
Ahab worshiped Baal.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֙ הֲנָקֵ֣ל לֶכְתּ֔וֹ בְּחַטֹּ֖אות יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־ נְבָ֑ט וַיִּקַּ֨ח אִשָּׁ֜ה אֶת־ אִיזֶ֗בֶל בַּת־ אֶתְבַּ֙עַל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ צִידֹנִ֔ים וַיֵּ֙לֶךְ֙ וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֣ד אֶת־ הַבַּ֔עַל וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: First, Ahab set up an altar for Baal in the temple of Baal that he had built in Samaria.
passages.sermon:
Ahab was king of Israel.
Ahab did evil in the sight of the LORD.
Ahab built a temple for Baal in Samaria.
Ahab set up an altar for Baal inside this temple.
passages.original: וַיָּ֥קֶם מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לַבָּ֑עַל בֵּ֣ית הַבַּ֔עַל אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּנָ֖ה בְּשֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Then he set up an Asherah pole. Thus Ahab did more to provoke the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger than all the kings of Israel before him.
passages.sermon:
Ahab was king of Israel.
Ahab set up an Asherah pole.
Ahab did things that made the LORD, the God of Israel, angry.
Ahab made the LORD angrier than any king of Israel before him.
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אַחְאָ֖ב אֶת־ הָאֲשֵׁרָ֑ה וַיּ֨וֹסֶף אַחְאָ֜ב לַעֲשׂ֗וֹת לְהַכְעִיס֙ אֶת־ יְהֹוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִכֹּ֨ל מַלְכֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֖וּ לְפָנָֽיו׃

passages.text: In Ahab’s days, Hiel the Bethelite rebuilt Jericho. At the cost of Abiram his firstborn he laid its foundation, and at the cost of Segub his youngest he set up its gates, according to the word that the LORD had spoken through Joshua son of Nun.
passages.sermon:
Ahab was king of Israel during this time.
Hiel was from Bethel.
Hiel rebuilt the city of Jericho.
Hiel laid the foundation of Jericho when his firstborn son, Abiram, died.
Hiel set up the gates of Jericho when his youngest son, Segub, died.
This happened as the LORD had spoken.
The LORD gave this word through Joshua son of Nun.
passages.original: בְּיָמָ֞יו בָּנָ֥ה חִיאֵ֛ל בֵּ֥ית הָאֱלִ֖י אֶת־ יְרִיחֹ֑ה בַּאֲבִירָ֨ם בְּכֹר֜וֹ יִסְּדָ֗הּ וּבִשְׂגִיב צְעִירוֹ֙ הִצִּ֣יב דְּלָתֶ֔יהָ כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּיַ֖ד יְהוֹשֻׁ֥עַ בִּן־ נֽוּן׃ס
